terms.usage: Interoceptomics is the standard name in prose and on GitHub.

scope_note: Names and definitions identify the programme and its scope. They do not establish a validated model or any biological or clinical capability.
release_policy: Each new version replaces the one before it on the main branch; Git history keeps the earlier ones. Experimental previews are published with their known limits. Publishing a version does not mean it has been validated.
license_note: The project's own work is CC0-1.0. The atlas anatomy (CC BY 4.0), guide recordings from people and a rat (CC BY 4.0), Three.js (MIT) and the fonts embedded in the script PDFs keep their own terms. See RIGHTS.md.

atlas_viewer.edition: Interoceptomics Atlas Viewer, version of 21 November 2026

package_manifest.scope: Sizes and checksums of the 73 other files in the archive, the counts recomputed from its data, and the identities of the upstream files.

atlas_viewer.change: The viewer is also served on the project website, from the same files. On the screen, one word for one thing (region, atlas number, cut) and controls that say what they do; links from the viewer to its guide and licence pages; a plain message when the page is opened straight from a folder. The start file serves the whole download folder. The anatomy and the controls are those of the previous version.

source_comparison.status: The region names were compared with the atlas table on an early edition and again on this version (21 November 2026): all 141 match on number, name, abbreviation and ancestry. The comparison with the API response was made once and cannot be repeated from the download.

atlas_viewer.limitations: The 3D model holds 121 of the atlas's 141 regions in 44 surfaces: 34 regions have a surface of their own, 82 more are parts of combined surfaces, and 5 are listed by name only. 20 regions have no surface. The source is one population atlas, left half only. Not checked or not claimed: agreement with other specimens, fit to any person, neural function, one planned visual check, and running on Windows, macOS or a phone.

viewer.code_change: Its drawing has not changed since the three flat cuts through one point were added. In this version only words changed: the loading message, the four view descriptions and one error message.

atlas_viewer.launchers: The Windows, macOS and Linux start files need Python 3.10 or newer and a browser with WebGL. The Linux start file served the tested viewer on the local machine. Opening the default browser, and running on Windows or macOS, have not been tried.

red_nucleus.evidence: Exact atlas-derived geometry independently checked. Comparison to separate MRI and histology remains qualitative.

vpl.evidence: The mesh shows one population-reference atlas boundary. Individual anatomy and neural function require separate evidence.

vpm.evidence: The surface gives one atlas boundary. Individual anatomy and neural function require separate evidence.

vpl_vpm_comparison.face_rule: Count each left annotation voxel face with labels 10424 and 10425 on opposite sides once. Edge and corner contacts are excluded.
vpl_vpm_comparison.evidence_scope: Atlas-label face adjacency in that source version. External tissue and MRI comparison is qualitative.
vpl_vpm_comparison.geometry: The VPL and VPM surface files and their matrices are unchanged since the edition that added the VPM surface.

shared_face_grid.native_coordinate_frame: Allen v1.0.0 original left, RAS mm. World metres (−R, S, A)/1000.
shared_face_grid.scope: Face-adjacency on the original 0.5 mm Allen v1.0.0 left annotation. Grid faces approximate an atlas boundary. No mesh intersection, individual anatomy, or neural connectivity is measured.

source_sections.native_coordinate_frame: Source-left Allen v1.0.0 RAS mm, world metres (−R, S, A)/1000
source_sections.section_scope: Exact labels 10424 and 10425 at original voxel centres. Other cells masked.

parietal_operculum.source_frame: Original v1.0.0 in ICBM 2009b Nonlinear Symmetric, native RAS millimetres
parietal_operculum.scope: Gross source label. Anatomy only. Histology and touch research are separately cited.

source_sections.scope: All native layers containing PaO, drawing original annotation IDs in each full plane. Only the original left PaO mesh is isolated in the 3D view.

annotation_planes.sampling: No interpolation. The x-fast native label array supplies one exact categorical ID per pixel.

axes.coronal: R increases rightward and S increases upward
axes.sagittal: A increases rightward and S increases upward
axes.axial: R increases rightward and A increases upward

annotation_planes.coordinate_units: NIfTI qform RAS millimetres, at voxel centre
annotation_planes.saved_view_version: atlas-labels-v1 for standard colour, atlas-labels-v2 for a highlighted selection
annotation_planes.mesh_window: Source-left 3D frame. The coordinate cross requires a labelled left voxel.

selected_label.count: Exact native ID across the full registered annotation. Side is classified by RAS voxel centre. Zero is unlabelled. Child IDs are separate.
selected_label.volume: Count multiplied by the absolute determinant of the verified axis-aligned 0.5 mm native qform (0.125 mm³).
selected_label.highlight: Every matching pixel on the three displayed planes, with separate counts per cut.

region_finder.source: Original ID at the native voxel. Midline is voxel-centre R = 0 mm. No alias or descendant substitution.
region_finder.selection: Nearest occupied voxel to the same-ID, same-side centroid in millimetres. Lowest native flat index breaks exact ties.

viewer_check.scope: Run for this version on Linux in headless Chromium with software rendering, from the download's start file and from a copy of docs/ served on this computer: the first view, a colour overlay, the parietal operculum shown alone, the three flat cuts, and the viewer page opened straight from the folder. The 3D model is the same picture, pixel for pixel, in both. Not run: hardware rendering, real keyboard, mouse and touch input, saved views, the published website itself, Windows, macOS, a phone.

version_of_19_november_2026.what: The edition this version carries its anatomy and code over from.
renderers: ANGLE (AMD, Vulkan 1.4.354 (AMD Radeon 8060S Graphics (RADV STRIX_HALO) (0x00001586)), radv)
version_of_19_november_2026.scope: The original Allen annotation and metadata were checked against all 170 occupied label-and-side combinations across 141 distinct IDs. The 3D preview covers the source left. Sparse source-right labels can be read in the cuts. Linux Chromium checks included the hardware and software renderers, keyboard input, emulated touch, saved views and the ruler. Native Windows, macOS and physical mobile checks remain open.

largest_file.note: Over 50 MB, where GitHub warns; under 100 MB, where it refuses.

website_copy.made_from: The archive's own members, by the same build. The viewer's folder is merged with the top level of the download, relative links in the pages are rewritten to match, and the four start files are left out. Every other byte is the archive's.

recorded_cortex.scope: Electrical band-power changes during finger cues versus following blank periods in one participant. The public reader loads the original anatomical surface and positions on request from Stanford or an exact local file.

cortical_coverage.scope: Regional coverage for 278 retained contacts in five preselected FingerFlex participants. Their deposited cortical surfaces, positions and anatomical labels open on demand. Each display keeps the participant’s native coordinates and camera.

stride_signals.scope: Group means from 89 barefoot C2 strides in 30 adults. The 52 marker paths and eight right-leg muscle channels share a stride clock. Physical plate means have different denominators. A separate right-foot force trace spans 2–58% of the stride from four qualified strides in three adults.
stride_signals.model_limits: The body surface illustrates marker motion. Plate forces sample contact on the instrumented walkway. The display aligns published filtered recordings retrospectively.

scalp_and_arm.scope: 61 scalp sites on the FieldTrip standard head, with four post-cue quarter-second windows summarizing 18 repeated trials per cue in one person across three runs. Eye sensors (62–64) and elbow, forearm and index-finger sensors appear separately. The 3D right arm illustrates the instruction. EEG and eye channels sample at 512 Hz and mechanical channels at 64 Hz. Individual traces, personal cap coordinates, calibrated physical arm units and hardware synchronization are outside this reader.
